channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbek President and Indian Prime Minister agree to elevate relations to new level
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi held talks in Tashkent, agreeing to elevate bilateral relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership. Trade turnover exceeded $1 billion last year, and joint ventures have increased sevenfold. Cooperation in education and cultural-humanitarian ties, including yoga, was also discussed.

item.title: New laboratory for geological sample analysis opens at NGMK Exploration Expedition
item.description: A modern laboratory for geological sample analysis has been commissioned at the Navoi Mining and Metallurgical Combinat (NGMK) Exploration Expedition. The new facility can analyze up to 400 geological samples daily, enabling a unified technological chain from drilling to 3D modeling and resource assessment. Over 50 new jobs were created.

item.title: Tashkent region and Anhui province expand cooperation in agriculture and agrobiotechnology
item.description: The Tashkent region and China's Anhui province are expanding cooperation, focusing on agriculture. Discussions included joint projects on water-saving irrigation, smart greenhouses, and In-Vitro laboratories for climate-resilient crops. Agrobiotechnology, silkworm farming, and personnel training were also identified as promising areas for collaboration.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister Awarded "Order of Friendship" in Uzbekistan
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi was awarded the "Order of Friendship" at the Kuksaroy residence. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev stated the award signifies the Uzbek people's high esteem for Modi's invaluable contribution to strengthening age-old friendship between the two nations.

item.title: International Media Forum in Uzbekistan Discusses Modernizing Islamic Civilization Narrative
item.description: An international media forum in Uzbekistan brought together nearly 300 media representatives and experts from 50 countries to discuss presenting Islamic civilization's history to a modern audience. Discussions focused on using digital tools and media to convey the legacy's relevance to contemporary education, technology, and culture.

item.title: Bishkek Mayor Pledges Aid to Victims of Madina Market Fire
item.description: Bishkek Mayor Aybek Dzhunushaliev met with traders at the site of the Madina market fire. He stated that authorities will identify and assist those affected by the blaze. The mayor urged people to allow emergency services to work and confirmed the market would not close on August 1, offering traders more time to relocate.

item.title: Uzbekistan Officials Warn Against Abolishing UzIMEI Payment System
item.description: Officials in Uzbekistan warn that abolishing the UzIMEI mobile device registration payment system could harm the state budget. The system has collected over 3 trillion soms to date. Transitioning to a system without payments would ultimately deplete state funds, according to the Republican Center for Telecommunication Network Management.

item.title: Chinese Workers Relocated in Bishkek After Mass Brawl
item.description: Chinese citizens temporarily working in Bishkek will be relocated following a mass brawl at their dormitory. Construction company representatives agreed to move the workers to reduce tensions. Twenty foreign workers were detained after the August 28 incident and will be deported from Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Not Fully Utilizing Investment Potential of Gulf Countries, Economist Says
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has established a strong political foundation for relations with Gulf countries but is not fully utilizing its investment potential, according to economist Shakhnos Gapurbayeva. While contacts have intensified, the focus needs to shift to concrete commercial projects to attract significant private and sovereign capital.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi Awarded Uzbekistan's Order of Friendship
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi received Uzbekistan's Order of High Friendship during a ceremony in Tashkent. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev presented the award, citing Modi's contributions to strengthening bilateral ties. Discussions during the visit focused on elevating relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership.

item.title: Chinese President Xi Jinping Arrives in Kyrgyzstan for State Visit and SCO Summit
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan were ceremonially welcomed at Manas International Airport in Bishkek. They were greeted by President Sadyr Japarov and First Lady Aigul Japarova. Xi Jinping is in Kyrgyzstan for a state visit and to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Foreign Minister: SCO is a key center for multipolar world order
item.description: The Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) has become a major transregional international organization, according to Kyrgyzstan's Foreign Minister Jeenbek Kulubaev. He stated in an interview that the SCO is a key center for forming a multipolar world order, emphasizing its platform for equal dialogue and mutual respect. Kyrgyzstan and China contribute significantly to the organization's development. The SCO summit will be held in Bishkek from August 31 to September 1.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan views China as a reliable and predictable partner, says Foreign Minister
item.description: Kyrgyzstan consistently views China as a reliable and predictable partner, according to Foreign Minister Jeenbek Kulubaev. He stated that the comprehensive strategic partnership between the two countries will be strengthened, benefiting their peoples and contributing to regional peace and stability. Kulubaev highlighted intensive political dialogue and cooperation in trade, economy, investment, transport, energy, and agriculture.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India agree to increase trade turnover to $5 billion by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan and India have agreed to increase their bilateral trade turnover to $5 billion by 2030. The agreement was reached during talks between Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Tashkent. Discussions focused on elevating cooperation to a comprehensive strategic partnership level and addressing key issues in trade, economy, investment, and humanitarian spheres.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India agree to boost mutual trade to $5 billion by 2030
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi held talks, agreeing to elevate bilateral relations to comprehensive strategic partnership. They aim to increase mutual trade turnover to $5 billion by 2030. Last year, trade exceeded $1 billion, with the number of joint ventures increasing sevenfold.

item.title: Bishkek mayor inspects city infrastructure ahead of SCO and VIC summits
item.description: Bishkek Mayor Aybek Dzhunushaliev inspected key city infrastructure and routes to Manas International Airport in preparation for upcoming international events, including the SCO and VIC summits. He focused on road reconstruction and general upkeep, emphasizing coordinated efforts and accountability among municipal services.

item.title: Nepal Flood Death Toll Reaches 734, Identification Difficulties Arise
item.description: The death toll from floods in Nepal has reached 734, with difficulties in identifying victims due to the large number of deceased and bodies being washed hundreds of kilometers away. Additionally, 2,498 people are missing, including 589 foreign nationals. Efforts are underway to identify the victims.

item.title: Kazatomprom Contributes to Uranium Sector Student Development with New University Office
item.description: Kazatomprom has opened a specialized office at the Kazakhstan-British Technical University (KBTU) for students in the "Uranium Business" program. The office will facilitate practical learning, project work, and industry expert meetings, bridging the gap between academia and real production. The program, launched in 2025, has seen a significant increase in student enrollment.

item.title: Tashkent schools to use AI to analyze student behavior and psychological state
item.description: Tashkent schools will implement an AI system to analyze student behavior and psychological state due to a rise in juvenile crime. The 'Smart School' project involves installing smart cameras in classrooms. This initiative aims to identify at-risk youth early and strengthen preventative measures.

item.title: Market fires caused by overloaded electrical networks and improper gas use, says Emergency Situations Ministry
item.description: Fires in Uzbek markets are primarily caused by overloaded electrical networks, not arson, according to the Deputy Minister of Emergency Situations. Increased use of appliances by vendors overloads older wiring, leading to overheating and fires, especially in hot weather. Improper gas cylinder use also contributes.

item.title: Uzbekistan Citizens' Travel to Turkey Increased by 17.7% Year-on-Year
item.description: In January-July of this year, over 166,000 citizens of Uzbekistan traveled to Turkey. This figure represents a 17.7% increase compared to the same period last year, indicating a rise in travel between the two countries.

item.title: Kazakhstan Offers Food Aid and Gaza Reconstruction Support to Palestine
item.description: Kazakhstan has expressed readiness to provide practical assistance to the Palestinian people, including food aid and participation in Gaza's reconstruction. Deputy Foreign Minister Arman Isagaliyev stated this at an Organization of Islamic Cooperation meeting. Kazakhstan supports a political resolution to the conflict based on the "two states for two peoples" formula.

item.title: China-Nepal Border Landslide: 16 Dead, 546 Missing; Climate Change Cited
item.description: A landslide on the China-Nepal border has resulted in 16 deaths and 546 missing persons. Experts attribute the disaster to glacier instability caused by long-term climate warming. Chinese authorities have allocated over $30 million for rescue efforts, with over 2,000 rescuers on site. 261 foreign nationals are among the missing.

item.title: Fire at Bishkek's 'Madina' Market Localized Over 400 Square Meters
item.description: A fire at the 'Madina' market in Bishkek has been localized, affecting approximately 400 square meters. Emergency services are working to extinguish remaining hotspots in containers. The preliminary cause is suspected to be a short circuit.

item.title: All Bishkek Fire Trucks Deployed to Combat 'Madina' Market Blaze
item.description: All available fire trucks in Bishkek were deployed to fight a large fire at the 'Madina' market. The fire, which started in a container and spread to stalls, is believed to have been caused by a short circuit. No injuries were reported.

item.title: Dengue Fever Cases Surge 85% in Afghanistan, WHO Reports
item.description: The World Health Organization reports an 85% increase in dengue fever cases in Afghanistan. The surge, along with rises in coronavirus and other infectious diseases, is straining the country's healthcare system due to seasonal outbreaks and shortages of medicine and resources.

item.title: US woman kills child to prevent father gaining custody
item.description: A woman in the United States has killed her child to prevent the father from gaining custody. The mother was reportedly unhappy about the father being granted parental rights and had previously abducted the child.

item.title: Afghanistan border crossing closures reduce Pakistan-Tajikistan trade by 70%
item.description: The closure of Afghanistan's border crossings has led to a nearly 70% reduction in trade between Pakistan and Tajikistan. Exports from Pakistan to Tajikistan fell by 61.3% to $11.9 million, while imports decreased by 82.8% to $3.3 million.

item.title: SCO Summit in 2026 to Emphasize 'Shanghai Spirit' Amid Global Transformation
item.description: The 2026 Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit will focus on the 'Shanghai Spirit'—mutual trust, benefit, equality, consultation, respect for diversity, and common development—amidst global changes, unilateralism, and bloc confrontation. The SCO emphasizes non-alignment and resolving disputes through dialogue, countering terrorism and cyber threats.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan at 35: Reflecting on independence, responsibility, and personal growth
item.description: As Kyrgyzstan marks 35 years of independence, the author reflects on the nation's journey, comparing it to reaching an age where personal responsibility replaces blaming external circumstances. The piece explores freedom, accountability, and the realization of potential.

item.title: Nazarali Aripov Appointed Kyrgyzstan's Ambassador to Tajikistan
item.description: Nazarali Aripov has been appointed as the new Ambassador of Kyrgyzstan to Tajikistan. President Sadyr Japarov signed the decree. Aripov previously served as Consul General in Almaty from May 2021 to June 2024. He replaces Erlan Abdyldaev, who was ambassador since April 2022.

item.title: Kazakhstan Schools Face Overcrowding with 380,000 First-Graders
item.description: Kazakhstan's schools are preparing for over 380,000 first-graders this academic year, raising concerns about class sizes and teacher workload. An Almaty teacher noted that large classes hinder individual attention and teaching quality, advocating for classes of 12-15 students.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank maintains interest rate amid inflation concerns
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank has kept its key interest rate at 12 percent due to external instability and geopolitical conflicts impacting the domestic market. Inflation has reached 7.3 percent year-to-date, with food prices up 6.3 percent. The bank aims to curb inflation by maintaining tight monetary conditions.

item.title: US Plans to Cut Off Egypt's Second Largest Bank from Global Financial System
item.description: The Trump administration is reportedly preparing new measures to increase financial pressure on Iran and its allies. If sanctions take effect, Banque Misr's UAE branch will be prohibited from conducting US dollar transactions. This move aims to isolate Egypt's second-largest bank from the international financial system.

item.title: Global media highlights Bishkek's role in upcoming SCO summit and World Nomad Games
item.description: International media is focusing on Bishkek ahead of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit and the World Nomad Games. Outlets like AFP view the SCO as a counterweight to Western influence, while others analyze regional dynamics and Kyrgyzstan's ambition to host major international events.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister arrives in Uzbekistan for state visit
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Uzbekistan for a state visit at the invitation of President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. He was welcomed at Tashkent-Humo International Airport by the Uzbek President. State flags and an honor guard were present for the occasion.

item.title: Chinese magazine features Uzbekistan's 35th independence anniversary
item.description: A special issue of China's 'Luokai' magazine highlights Uzbekistan's 35th independence anniversary, detailing reforms and achievements in politics, economy, and culture. It covers bilateral cooperation, investment potential, the Islamic Civilization Center, and the 'Uzbekistan-2030' strategy.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India's Strategic Partnership Shows Growing Momentum
item.description: Uzbek-Indian relations have gained new momentum since 2017, evolving beyond political dialogue to multifaceted practical cooperation. This strategic partnership spans politics, economy, industry, health, digital sectors, education, security, and transport, driven by political will and complementary economies.

item.title: Russia's Foreign Ministry Calls Armenia's Mobilization Statements a Provocation
item.description: Russia's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova labeled statements by Armenian Security Council Secretary Alen Simonyan regarding accepting Russians in case of mobilization as a provocation. Zakharova stated Simonyan's remarks encourage illegal actions and politicize Armenian hospitality. The ministry expressed regret over Yerevan's public statements undermining bilateral cooperation with Moscow.

item.title: Uzbekistan Presents Parliamentary Diplomacy Experience at Phnom Penh Conference
item.description: Uzbekistan shared its parliamentary diplomacy experience at the II Inter-Parliamentary Conference in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. The delegation highlighted the strengthening atmosphere of good neighborliness and cooperation in Central Asia, emphasizing constructive dialogue for conflict resolution.
